named_subject: a lion lying down, drawn as a round smiling face inside a spiky mane with a long low body
action: The camera pans right past one resting lion, which slides off to the right, and a second resting lion enters from the left and settles in the lower left of the frame.
identity_gap: In frames 10 to 16 the black lion matches the doodle's spiky mane, smiling oval face and open looped body, but in frames 1 to 7 the same drawing appears only in grey as scenery, and in frame 8 only a detached black mane fragment is shown.
notes: The layout and pan follow the film closely, but the black character first appears in frame 8 as an isolated mane piece and then jumps to a partial lion at the left edge in frame 9, so the entrance pops instead of sliding in. The change that would help most is to bring the second lion in from the left edge as one whole drawing that moves in steadily over frames 8 to 10, instead of a fragment that appears mid-frame.
